title: GST, invoices and BAS
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:39Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point only teaches calculating GST on a price (adding 10% or finding the GST in a GST-inclusive price), while the new point is about invoices and reporting GST collected and paid on a business activity statement (BAS), which the card does not cover.

draft.title: GST, invoices and BAS
card: GST
GST is the goods and services tax. It is 10% of the price of most goods and services in Australia.
Invoice
A business adds GST to the price on an invoice. Price without GST × 1.1 gives the price with GST. Price with GST ÷ 11 gives the GST part.
BAS
A business activity statement (BAS) reports the GST a business collected from customers and the GST it paid on its own purchases.
Amount owed
GST collected − GST paid = amount sent to the tax office. Example: collected $900 and paid $400 gives 900 − 400 = $500 to send.
draft.remember: GST is 10% added to the price, and the BAS works out collected minus paid.

a.q: Kofi's workshop charges $350 for a job, before GST. What is the invoice total including GST?
a.why: GST is 10% of 350 = $35, so the total is 350 + 35 = $385. $35 is only the GST, not the total.
a.clue: Work out 10% of the price, then add it on.

b.q: Lena's bakery collected $2200 GST from customers and paid $1500 GST on supplies this quarter. What does her BAS show she sends to the tax office?
b.why: The amount sent is GST collected minus GST paid: 2200 − 1500 = $700. Adding them to get $3700 is wrong because the GST paid on supplies is taken off.
b.clue: Take away the GST the business paid.
